initial: I need to book a restaurant for a work dinner.
complication: Two things: first, the VP insists it must be a traditional steakhouse — no vegetarian-focused menus. Second, two of our guests are strict vegetarians who need substantial plant-based options. These might conflict — can you find somewhere that satisfies both?
pivot: We've decided to go ahead. Book the steakhouse and add a note about the vegetarian requirements. The VP is aware. Keep all other details the same.

initial: Help me book somewhere special for a dinner.

clarification_drip.dietary|allerg|vegan|vegetarian: one person has a severe fish allergy

complication: I just realized — omakase is almost entirely fish-based, but one of our guests has a severe fish allergy. I still want omakase but also need it to be fish-free for one person. Is that possible?
pivot: The guest with the fish allergy is fine having a completely separate non-omakase meal at the same restaurant. Please book the omakase for 5 and a separate menu for 1. Still Friday, 8 PM, New York.
post_booking_probes: Is the omakase noted for 5 and separate menu for 1?

initial: I want to plan a big celebration dinner.
complication: My uncle insists it must be a halal-certified restaurant — he won't come otherwise. But the vegan guests specifically want a place that also has strong vegan credentials. Some halal places are meat-heavy and don't cater well to vegans. Can you find somewhere that is both halal-certified AND has an extensive vegan menu?
pivot: My uncle confirmed he will attend regardless. Prioritise vegan options and just note halal preferred. 20 people, Indian, San Francisco, Saturday, 7 PM.

initial: I need to book somewhere for a team event.
complication: Korean BBQ typically mixes meat and other items on the same grills, which violates kosher rules. But the team really wants Korean BBQ. The kosher guests say they'd need a separate certified kosher option. Can you handle both?
pivot: The kosher guests have agreed to eat beforehand and just join for drinks. Book the Korean BBQ for all 15 but note that 4 guests won't be eating and need non-alcoholic drink service only. Thursday, 6:30 PM, Los Angeles.
post_booking_probes: Is the note about 4 non-eating guests included?

initial: I need to book flights for a group of colleagues.
complication: Our CFO says we must book the cheapest available economy seats. But our HR policy requires all flights over 6 hours to be economy plus for duty-of-care reasons. New York to London is 7 hours. These two policies directly conflict. How do you want me to handle this?
pivot: HR policy takes precedence — book economy plus for everyone. The CFO has been informed. 10 passengers, New York to London, March 15th to March 22nd.
post_booking_probes: What cabin class did we book?

initial: I need to book flights for a conference trip.
complication: I want to arrive September 5th for a 9 AM meeting, but the only direct business class flight from Chicago arrives September 5th at 11 PM local time — too late for the meeting. The flight that arrives in time departs September 3rd and is economy only. I need to be there for the 9 AM meeting AND I want business class. These can't both happen on the same flight. What do you suggest?
pivot: I'll take the September 3rd economy flight so I make the meeting. The meeting matters more than comfort. Change departure to September 3rd, economy class, still returning September 12th.
post_booking_probes: Is the vegan meal still noted?

initial: I need to arrange family flights for summer vacation.

clarification_drip.baggage|luggage|bags|checked: two checked bags for the family

complication: My husband insists we fly non-stop only — he gets anxious on connections. But July 1st non-stop Miami to Paris is sold out in economy. The only non-stop available is business class at 3x the price. Economy has seats but with a connection in New York. What do we do?
pivot: We'll take the connection — the price difference is too much. Economy with connection via New York, July 1st, still returning July 15th. 4 passengers, child meals for both kids.
post_booking_probes: Are child meals noted for both kids?
